findings.title: Light-theme value for embedded-post link color changed from 30% to 70%
findings.body: The original rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new rule is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. The light-theme branch moved from 30% to 70%, so `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` is now much fainter on light themes. This PR is meant to leave light themes unchanged and only fix dark themes. It looks like the dark-theme pair (30%) was copied into the light slot. The correct pair is `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)`.

findings.title: `.group-member-info .name` light color changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: The original color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new rule uses 50%/50%. That makes the name text lighter on light themes and drops the visual distinction between `.name` and `.title`, which now share the same color. The light-theme appearance changes unintentionally. The pair should be 30% for `$primary` and 70% for `$secondary`.

findings.title: `.custom-message-length` light-theme color inverted from 70% to 30%
findings.body: The original color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The new rule is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The light branch now uses 30%, so the hint text is much darker on light themes. The pair is swapped relative to the desktop `.custom-message-length` rule in this same PR, which correctly uses 70%/30%. Mobile and desktop now diverge. It should be `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` and `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)`.

findings.title: Topic map `h3` color changed from 20% to 50%/50%, altering the light theme
findings.body: The original `.topic-map h3` color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. The new rule is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme value goes from 20% to 50%, so the heading is noticeably lighter and loses contrast against its `h4` sibling. The matching desktop rule in this PR correctly uses 20%/80%. This one should be `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` and `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%)`.

findings.title: Mobile `.group-member-info .name` light color changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: The original color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new rule uses 50%/50%. This changes the light-theme appearance and makes `.name` identical to `.title`. It repeats the same mistake as in desktop/user.scss. The pair should be 30% for `$primary` and 70% for `$secondary`.

findings.title: Missed conversion: categories badge-notification still uses a bare `scale-color($primary, ...)`
findings.body: `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` still has `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%);` with no `dark-light-choose`. On dark themes `$primary` is light, so scaling it 50% towards white gives poor contrast. That is exactly the bug this PR fixes elsewhere. The same file's other 50% usages were converted, so this one should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))` too.
